bc_tippling_tower.blurb: Tippling Tower is a small sport crag tucked into the Doctors' Group at Skaha Bluffs, above Penticton in the Okanagan. Ten bolted lines climb an airy, overhanging tower, so the character is steep and a little exposed rather than relaxed. The grades start at a single 5.9 and then climb steadily: a few 5.10s, a cluster of 5.11s, and a handful of 5.12 and 5.13 routes at the top end. That makes it best for confident leaders who want something harder than the beginner walls nearby. It sits in the north end of the Doctors' Wall gully, and the walk in from the main trail is short but steep. Spring and autumn suit it best.

bc_the_east_portal.blurb: The East Portal is a compact cliff in the Doctors' Group at Skaha Bluffs, facing the main Doctors' Wall across a gully. Ten routes here are mostly trad, with just two sport lines, and the quality and the style of protection vary quite a bit from one line to the next. The grades run from 5.9 up to the low 5.12s, with a good block of 5.9s and another of 5.11s. Expect to place gear low down on some routes, which keeps the crowds thin. The south-facing wall catches plenty of sun, though large trees throw shade over parts of the base and the lower pitches.

bc_grassy_glades.blurb: Grassy Glades is one of the Small Eastern Crags at Skaha Bluffs near Penticton, a west-facing wall with ten routes, nearly all of them bolted sport lines and one trad crack. It is a gentle place to warm up: a handful of lines fall in the low 5.6 to 5.8 range, then a few 5.10s and a pair of 5.11s offer something steeper. Climbs finish at chains or rap rings. It makes a handy stop on the way to Morning Glory, or an easier alternative before heading to the harder walls, and it tends to be busy on weekends. The walk in from the upper lot takes roughly half an hour.

bc_lower_road_side_wall.blurb: Lower Road Side Wall is a short limestone sport wall at Slesse Creek in the Chilliwack Lake Road corridor of the Fraser Valley. It stands only a few steps off the road, so there is almost no walk. All ten routes are bolted sport lines, and the grades sit in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, with the 5.11s and 5.12s making up most of the list. Expect short pitches with hard starts, and the first bolts were placed low enough to be clipped with a stick. The limestone has coral-like pockets and can feel sharp in places; belayers should wear a helmet because small pieces can come down.

bc_zunga_bouldering_wall.blurb: Zunga Bouldering Wall is a small overhanging boulder wall in the Chehalis River Gorge near Agassiz, sitting just above the better-known Zunga Wall. The rock is very smooth and steep, with open-hand slopers mixed with big jugs, and it faces south in shade. The few boulder problems run from an easy traverse through the V4 to V6 range, so it suits intermediate to strong boulderers, and extra pads help under the overhangs. Beyond the problems, the gorge also holds a few sport, trad and top-rope lines around 5.9 to 5.12. A quiet spot, usually without crowds, and the walk from the lower wall is only a short way along a side trail.
